## Step order

`sw_clean_run()` runs the cleaning stage of the validated pipeline order in
one call. It takes FCS paths, a flowFrame, a flowSet or a list of
flowFrames, and runs these steps in this order:

1. Margin events are removed on the raw scale. `margin_range` sets the
   limits for the fluorescence channels; scatter keeps the FCS range.
   PeacoQC reads a lower limit above 0 as 0, so a `margin_range[1]` above 0
   gives a warning and the run continues.
2. All fluorescence channels get an arcsinh transformation. Scatter stays raw.
3. PeacoQC removes unstable signal.
4. The `nonDebris` gate removes the low FSC-A cloud.
5. The `singlets` gate keeps events on the FSC-A against FSC-H diagonal.
6. The `live` gate keeps events below the viability cut.

Nothing runs after the live gate: there is no CD3 or lymphocyte gate.
A sample with no events left after any step stops the run, with the sample
and the step named.

### Missing arguments stop the run

Ten values change the counts and the cuts, so all ten are required
arguments with no default. A call that leaves any out stops once, before any
step runs. The message lists every missing value with what it controls, how to
choose it and the benchmark 05 reference value. The reference is a test
value, not a recommendation. This chunk calls the function with only the data
and prints the message it returns.

```{r}
#| label: clean-synthetic-frame
# Synthetic cells, debris (low FSC-A), doublets (low FSC-H for their FSC-A)
# and dead cells (high viability dye), in one in-memory flowFrame.
set.seed(1)
syn_n_cells <- 8000
syn_n_debris <- 600
syn_n_doublet <- 600
syn_n_dead <- 800

syn_fsc_a <- c(
  rnorm(syn_n_cells, 6e5, 3e4),
  rnorm(syn_n_debris, 5e4, 1.5e4),
  rnorm(syn_n_doublet, 6e5, 3e4),
  rnorm(syn_n_dead, 6e5, 3e4)
)
syn_n <- length(syn_fsc_a)
syn_fsc_h <- syn_fsc_a * 0.8 + rnorm(syn_n, 0, 8000)
syn_is_doublet <- seq_len(syn_n) %in%
  (syn_n_cells + syn_n_debris + seq_len(syn_n_doublet))
syn_fsc_h[syn_is_doublet] <- syn_fsc_a[syn_is_doublet] * 0.45
syn_viability <- c(
  rnorm(syn_n - syn_n_dead, 1000, 600),
  rnorm(syn_n_dead, 3e5, 5e4)
)

syn_mat <- cbind(
  "FSC-A" = syn_fsc_a,
  "FSC-H" = syn_fsc_h,
  "SSC-A" = abs(rnorm(syn_n, 1e5, 2e4)),
  "Time" = seq_len(syn_n) / 100,
  "BV421-A" = rnorm(syn_n, 2000, 800),
  "PE-A" = rnorm(syn_n, 3000, 900),
  "LIVE DEAD NIR-A" = syn_viability
)
# Mix the classes along the run, then restore a monotone Time.
syn_mat <- syn_mat[sample(syn_n), ]
syn_mat[, "Time"] <- seq_len(syn_n) / 100

syn_ff <- flowFrame(syn_mat)
syn_pd <- pData(parameters(syn_ff))
syn_pd$minRange <- -1e6
syn_pd$maxRange <- 4e6
pData(parameters(syn_ff)) <- syn_pd

# A named list gives the sample a stable name in the output tables.
syn_samples <- list(synthetic = syn_ff)
```

```{r}
#| label: clean-missing-args
# conditionMessage() returns the text of the error that sw_clean_run() raised.
clean_msg <- tryCatch(
  sw_clean_run(syn_samples),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
cat(clean_msg)
```

### Run it on the synthetic frame

The run below needs a value for each of the ten arguments. Every value in
the `clean_args` list is a placeholder that lets this synthetic frame run. It
is not a recommendation, and nothing in the package fills it in for you.
Choose each value for your own data, as the message above describes.

```{r}
#| label: clean-run
clean_args <- list(
  margin_range = c(-21761, 1e7), # placeholder for this synthetic run
  debris_window = c(1e4, 1.5e6), # placeholder for this synthetic frame
  singlet_wider_gate = TRUE, # placeholder: TRUE or FALSE
  pool_samples = TRUE, # placeholder: TRUE or FALSE
  viability_channel = "LIVE DEAD NIR-A", # placeholder: your dye channel
  viability_method = "mindensity", # placeholder: "mindensity" or "boundary"
  viability_cut = NULL, # NULL goes with "mindensity"
  IT_limit = 0.55, # placeholder: between 0 and 1
  MAD = 6, # placeholder: positive number
  cofactor = 6000 # placeholder: positive number
)

# The progress lines below come from PeacoQC and openCyto. PeacoQC warns that
# this small frame has too few bins for its isolation tree analysis; real
# files have more events.
clean_res <- do.call(sw_clean_run, c(list(x = syn_samples), clean_args))
names(clean_res)
```

### Audit table and gates

`audit` has one row per sample and step. `n_removed` is the number of events
that step removed, and `NA` for `raw`. The margin step removes the events at
the observed minimum and maximum of every scatter and fluorescence channel,
so it removes a few events even when none reach `margin_range` or the
instrument range. On real 40-colour Aurora files, look at the `margins` row
first. `margin_range` has no default. In a smoke run on 5 BMV files (A3, A6,
B11, B2, D1), made before `sw_clean_run()` had a margin argument, PeacoQC
printed "More than X % is considered as a margin event" warnings of 99.34 %
(A3), 99.81 % (A6), 99.48 % (B11), 99.16 % (B2) and 99.86 % (D1)
(`experiments/runs/2026-11-11_clean-run-smoke/warnings.txt`; git does not track
the run folder). A comment in
`experiments/benchmarks/05_bmv-unmix-compare/12_cleanup.R` records that PeacoQC
defaults removed 99.9% of events in benchmark 05. That is a different run, not
the same measurement.

```{r}
#| label: clean-audit
as.data.frame(clean_res$audit)
```

`gates` has one row per sample and gate. `definition` holds the rectangle
limits or the polygon vertices that were applied. `keeps` says whether the
gate keeps events inside or outside that shape: the `live` gate keeps events
outside the rectangle. `cut_at_window_floor` is filled for `nonDebris` rows
only.

```{r}
#| label: clean-gates
as.data.frame(clean_res$gates)
```

The per-sample PeacoQC summary and the arguments the run used are stored with
the result, so the run can be repeated from them.

```{r}
#| label: clean-qc-parameters
clean_res$qc
str(clean_res$parameters)
```

### What `debris_window` does

`debris_window = c(min, max)` sets the range of FSC-A values (raw scale) that
the `nonDebris` density is built from. openCyto drops the events outside
`[min, max]` before it looks for peaks and valleys. The cut is therefore a
valley of the density of the events inside the window, and it lies inside the
window. The cut is the deepest valley between the two highest peaks, or the
deepest valley overall if none lies between them.

The gate keeps events at or above the cut. Events below `min` are always
debris. Events above `max` are never removed by this gate. `max = Inf` means
no upper limit.

If the window holds one peak or no valley, openCyto puts the cut on the
lowest event inside the window. That removes nothing at or above `min`.
`sw_clean_run()` warns in this case and sets `cut_at_window_floor` to `TRUE`
in the `gates` table. A window that leaves out the valley you want can also
put the cut at a different valley inside it. So check the `nonDebris`
`definition` in `$gates` against the FSC-A density, as in the figure below.

```{r}
#| label: clean-debris-figure
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-cap: "Synthetic data. Raw FSC-A density of all synthetic events, with the debris_window limits and the nonDebris cut from $gates."
#| fig-alt: "Density of raw FSC-A with a small low-FSC debris peak and a large cell peak. Dashed lines mark the debris_window limits and a solid line marks the nonDebris cut, which lies between the two peaks."
library(ggplot2)

# The cut is the lower limit in the nonDebris definition, e.g. "FSC-A: [232684, Inf]".
debris_def <- clean_res$gates$definition[clean_res$gates$gate == "nonDebris"]
debris_cut <- as.numeric(sub("^FSC-A: \\[([^,]+),.*$", "\\1", debris_def))

# All events of the synthetic frame, before any step, on the raw scale.
fsc_plot <- data.frame(fsc_a = exprs(syn_ff)[, "FSC-A"])
window_limits <- data.frame(
  limit = c("debris_window min", "debris_window max", "nonDebris cut"),
  fsc_a = c(clean_args$debris_window, debris_cut)
)

ggplot(fsc_plot, aes(fsc_a)) +
  geom_density(fill = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(
    data = window_limits,
    aes(xintercept = fsc_a, linetype = limit)
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "debris_window min" = "dashed",
      "debris_window max" = "dashed",
      "nonDebris cut" = "solid"
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = "FSC-A (raw)", y = "Density", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9)
```

The figure uses synthetic data made in this vignette.

### Every value is yours

All ten values are the caller's choice, and the package gives no recommended
value for any of them. The benchmark 05 numbers in the error message are the
values that benchmark used as test values. They are not a recommendation. The
placeholders in `clean_args` serve this synthetic frame only. To choose a
value, follow the "How to choose" text in the message, and check the result in
the `audit` and `gates` tables before you use the cleaned events.
